_comment: A second amendment to G.4, written 2026-10-21. It changes no byte of
chip/PREREGISTRATION.json or of chip/PREREG_AMENDMENT.json, the first
amendment, and records both by hash. The first amendment left the
abstention rule as frozen. This one adds one condition to it, for one
reason found on 20 October: a second extractor run over the same
layout calls one of Arm A's six scored pairs level, where the SPEF
calls it by more than a percent.
preregister.py --amendment holds this file the way it holds the
first: its quotes against the two files it amends, the hashes it
records against the files on disk, and the scored pairs it lists
against the rule it states, worked again from the tables it names.
not_a_preregistration_why: PREREGISTRATION.json was frozen on 31 August and the first amendment
was written on 18 October, both before any of this was known. This
file was written after a second extraction of the layout, with its
numbers in hand. No die had been read and nothing had been measured,
so none of it can have been fitted to data, but it is a decision taken
late, and it must never be cited as though it carried the frozen

first.what: the release build's SPEF, the tables every prediction has been read from: Arms A and C through the archive's full RC decks, Arm B through its instance decks, the macro's own extraction the same for all sixteen with each instance's enable and output routes from the SPEF

second.what: magic's extraction of the same layout, capacitance only, through the archive's lumped deck, run on 20 October

amends.frozen_text: A pair whose frequency separation is below the high-margin threshold in TOLERANCES.json is an abstention.
amends.first_amendment_text: the abstention rule read from extraction/TOLERANCES.json
now: A pair is scored only if its separation clears the high-margin
line in extraction/TOLERANCES.json, with the same sign, in both
tables named above: the SPEF's, which the predictions are read
from, and magic's, a second extraction of the same layout through
lumped decks, since that extraction is capacitance only. Every
other pair is an abstention, counted and published, its sign never
scored either way. The line is read from TOLERANCES.json and not
re-derived, and a separation is f_a minus f_b as a percent of the
mean of that arm's sixteen rings in the same table. For a scored
pair the two tables agree on the sign, and that sign is the
prediction. The rule is the same for all three arms.
why: Every prediction in the project was read from one extraction, the
SPEF OpenRCX wrote. On 20 October the same layout went through
magic, which also sees inside the standard cells, and the ring
decks were run again with its loads. Five of Arm A's six scored
pairs come out the same way and over the line. Pair 0/1 does not:
the SPEF has ring 0 faster by 1.08 percent of the arm's mean,
magic has the two level, -0.015, and with metal fill ring 1
ahead. The SPEF puts 1.36 fF more on ring 1 than on ring 0, and
magic about a tenth of one. The SPEF's own lumped decks put pair
0/1 at +1.069, so the split is the extractor's and not the
resistance's.
The line already allows each ring an extraction error the size of
one ring's mismatch (T2a in TOLERANCES.json), as if an extraction
could be off by that much and no more. Two open extractors part on
pair 0/1 by about 1.3 fF. A call that turns on the choice of
extractor is a call about the tool and not about the layout, and
the line's own reasoning is that such a call is not scored: a
low-margin sign that comes out right is not a result, and one that
comes out wrong is not a failure.
As it stood, M1 on Arm A needed six of six, and one of the six was
a pair the two extractors call differently, with nothing in hand
to say which of them is right. The primary test would have turned
on that one pair.
gives_up: M1 on Arm A can no longer pass on its own. Five of five is 1/32,
0.03125, over the first Holm level, so it is tested at 0.05 only
after M4 has cleared 0.025, and if M4 fails it fails with it. Taken
knowing that M4, run through primary_tests.py on the model
frequencies, has p(1) of 0.0011 from the SPEF, 0.012 from magic and
at most 0.00011 with fill. With the 0.062 percent ring mismatch
drawn 200 times onto magic's frequencies it stayed under 0.025
every time, the largest 0.023. magic without fill is where tying
M1 to M4 costs the most.
Pair 0/1 scores nothing whichever way it comes out. Arm C's
secondary M1 loses 8/9 and 10/11, which magic puts under the line.
And the scored pairs now rest on a second tool's numbers as well
as the first's. They are in sim/spice/magic/ with the decks and
logs they came from, and recorded here by hash.
fill_left_out: Metal fill is not part of the rule. Whether Tiny Tapeout's fill
reaches inside the tile, and with which tool, is not known. With
the fill open_pdks' generator draws, at four grid positions, the
first run in SPICE and the other three moved from it by the fitted
fill slope, the five pairs Arm A scores keep their sign and stay
over the line in every one. None of Arm C's three does: 12/13
turns round, and 4/5 and 14/15 keep their sign but fall under the
line. M1 on Arm C is secondary and carries no claim.
decks_differ: The two tables are not the same kind of deck. The SPEF's side is
the RC decks the predictions come from, and magic's side is lumped,
the only kind a capacitance-only extraction gives. Like for like,
the SPEF's own lumped decks keep Arm A's five scored pairs over the
line with the same signs, and split on 0/1 the same way, +1.069
against magic's -0.015. They differ from the RC decks elsewhere:
they put 2/3 and 8/9 over the line, which the RC decks and the
frozen rule leave out, and Arm C's 4/5 and 14/15 under it, -0.588
and -0.602 where the RC decks have -1.322 and -0.648.

not_amended: The line itself and its derivation in extraction/TOLERANCES.json, the pairing, the bit convention, the two primaries and Holm over them, M1's test, the die M1 and M4 are tested on, and everything else in chip/PREREG_AMENDMENT.json stand as they are.
preregister.py P03 still reads the frozen abstention sentence and passes on it. The added condition is held by --amendment instead.
still_open: Whatever archive of the per-pair predictions is made before the first die is read takes the scored pairs above.

Everything still open in chip/PREREG_AMENDMENT.json is still open: the M4 secondary's interval, M2's shuffles and seed, E.3, and the paper's preregistration section, which now takes up both amendments.
